name: Mouth-blown cased opal (globes)
process: The gaffer blows a thin gather of clear glass, overlays it with a gather of opal, and (for triplex) with a further layer of clear, then blows the globe to shape in a mould or free, leaving a neck and rolled lip for the gallery. The opal layer sits between glossy clear skins: outside the globe mirrors the room like any glass; inside, the opal diffuses the lamp so that no filament shows. The thinner and more even the opal layer, the more light the globe passes.
